name: Shapham
overview: Shapham is a male figure from the tribe of Gad, recognized as the second chief among the Gadites. His leadership role is explicitly noted in the biblical record, highlighting his significance within his tribe. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shapham appears as a proper name in Scripture without a provided meaning or divine origin. It is simply identified as his personal name in 1 Chronicles 5:12.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shapham as a descendant of Gad, affirming his tribal lineage. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shapham's importance lies in his position as the second chief of the Gadites, indicating a leadership role within the tribe of Gad. This status underscores his responsibility and influence among his people during the period documented in 1 Chronicles. His mention in Scripture serves to preserve the genealogical and tribal organization important to the history of Israel.
